records.text: Blue Dynamics churned, flagging for the pipeline review

records.subject: Sorry to see you go
records.body:
Hi Ben,

Confirming the cancellation on our end. We're sorry Wrenfield didn't end up being the right fit for Blue Dynamics -- the door's open if that changes.

Cheers,
Priya Chen

records.subject: Picking back up with Wrenfield
records.body:
Hi Ben,

A lot of teams stall right at inviting their first teammate. If that's where things got stuck, a teammate can be invited from Account Settings -> Members at any time.

Cheers,
Priya Chen

records.subject: Checking in on Blue Dynamics' setup
records.body:
Hi Ben,

Noticed you created a project already, which is great. Anything unclear as you're digging in?

Cheers,
Priya Chen

records.subject: Welcome to Wrenfield, Blue Dynamics!
records.body:
Hi Ben,

Your Wrenfield account is live. A simple way to start: one project, a handful of real tasks, then an invite to a teammate. No need to overthink the setup.

Here if you need anything.

Cheers,
Priya Chen

decisions.rationale: Project reached day 1 ([email:6b7aaf8c] window), but no invite and no key milestone by day 6, and Ben never replied to either outreach ([email:c4ac5963]). Zero tickets suggests low engagement rather than blockers. Pro plan and early project creation give some upside; 8 days left.

draft.subject: One next step for Blue Dynamics
draft.body:
Hi Ben,

Following up on my note last week — you've got a project created, which is the main thing. In Wrenfield, projects are the main organizing unit, and tasks live inside them, so adding a few real tasks to that project is usually the fastest way to see whether it fits how your team works.

If it's useful, a teammate can be invited from Account Settings -> Members at any time, and teammates can be bulk-invited from a CSV file instead of one at a time.

Want me to walk through your first project with you on a 15-minute call this week?

Best,
Priya
